head: Google takes down a botnet of 1.3 million Android TV boxes
dek: Google led a takedown of a botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, in late October. Google says the maker Videostrong built a backdoor into the boxes on purpose and sold access to criminals.
details: The criminals used owners' home connections to pass other people's internet traffic and to fake ad views; the backdoor could also install apps silently and capture the screen. It's part of the boxes' firmware, so it can't be removed and comes back after a restart. Videostrong makes boxes under its own name and for other brands; Google has banned it from certified Android devices.
where: Android TV boxes worldwide; also some karaoke machines, telehealth devices and signs
means: If you use a cheap no-name Android TV box, it may be running a backdoor that uses your internet connection for strangers.
todo: If you own an Android TV box from a little-known brand: Plume recommends a full factory reset, and Synthient tells consumers to stop using such boxes for good, since the backdoor can't be removed by owners.
